blocks: Artificial intelligence is a new frontier of human development and a major driving force of the new round of scientific, technological and industrial transformation, and it can also be an international public good that benefits humanity. AI brings unprecedented opportunities for development, and also risks and challenges never met before. In the intelligent era, only by pulling together as one world can we unlock the full potential of AI while ensuring that its development is safe, reliable, controllable and fair, and ultimately deliver on the relevant commitments of the UN Pact for the Future and its annex, the Global Digital Compact, creating an inclusive, open, sustainable, fair, safe and reliable digital and intelligent future for all.

To this end, we put forward the Global AI Governance Action Plan, and call on all parties, on the basis of the goals and principles of AI for good and for the people, respect for sovereignty, a development orientation, safety and controllability, fairness and inclusiveness, and openness and cooperation, to take effective action in earnest and to advance global AI development and governance together.

1. Jointly seize the opportunities of AI. We call on all actors, including governments, international organisations, enterprises, research institutes and universities, civil-society organisations and individual citizens, to take an active part and work together: to accelerate the building of digital infrastructure, jointly explore frontier innovation in AI technology, promote the spread and application of AI worldwide, and release to the fullest AI’s great potential to empower global economic and social development, help implement the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, and respond to global challenges.

2. Promote innovative development of AI. In a spirit of openness and sharing, encourage bold experimentation and exploration; build international platforms for scientific and technological cooperation of every kind; foster an innovation-friendly policy environment; strengthen the coordination of policy and regulation; promote technical cooperation and the commercialisation of results; lower and remove technical barriers; jointly drive breakthroughs in AI technology and its sustained development; open up “AI+” application scenarios in depth; and raise the level of AI innovation and development worldwide.

3. Empower every industry with AI. Advance the use of AI in industrial manufacturing, consumption, trade and distribution, healthcare, education, agriculture, poverty reduction and other fields; promote deep application of AI in scenarios such as autonomous driving and smart cities; and build a rich, diverse and healthy AI application ecosystem oriented to the good. Advance the building and sharing of intelligent infrastructure, carry out cross-border cooperation on AI applications, exchange best practices, and jointly explore how AI can comprehensively empower the real economy.

4. Accelerate the building of digital infrastructure. Accelerate the building of global infrastructure for clean electricity, next-generation networks, intelligent computing power and data centres; improve the layout of interoperable AI and digital infrastructure; promote a unified system of computing-power standards; support all countries, the Global South in particular, in developing AI technologies and services suited to their own national conditions; help the Global South gain real access to AI and put it to use; and promote inclusive development of AI that benefits all.

5. Build a diverse and open innovation ecosystem. Give full play to governments, industry, academia and other actors, and to platforms and mechanisms, in jointly advancing international exchange and dialogue on AI governance; build cross-border open-source communities and safe, reliable open-source platforms; promote the open sharing of foundational resources; lower the threshold for technical innovation and application; avoid duplicated investment and wasted resources; and make AI technologies and services more inclusive and accessible. Build an open-source compliance system, define and implement technical security guidelines for open-source communities, promote the open sharing of development resources such as technical and interface documentation, strengthen open-source ecosystem building such as compatibility, adaptation and interconnection between upstream and downstream products, and allow non-sensitive technical resources to flow openly.

6. Actively expand the supply of high-quality data. Use high-quality data to drive AI development; cooperate in promoting the lawful, orderly and free flow of data; explore a global mechanism and platform for data sharing; and jointly build high-quality datasets to give AI development more to feed on. At the same time, actively safeguard personal privacy and data security, diversify AI training data and corpora, eliminate discrimination and bias, and promote, protect and preserve the diversity of AI ecosystems and of human civilisations.

7. Respond effectively to energy and environmental problems. Advocate the concept of “sustainable AI”; support continued exploration of resource-saving and environmentally friendly models of AI development; jointly set energy-efficiency and water-efficiency standards for AI; and promote green computing technologies such as low-power chips and efficient algorithms. Encourage dialogue and cooperation on energy saving in AI development, to find the best solutions together. Promote AI as an enabler of green transition, climate-change response, biodiversity protection and related fields, widen its application there, strengthen international cooperation and share best practices.

8. Promote consensus on standards and norms. Support dialogue among national standard-setting bodies; through international standards organisations such as the International Telecommunication Union, the International Organization for Standardization and the International Electrotechnical Commission, and with due weight given to the role of industry, accelerate the drafting and revision of technical standards in key areas such as safety, industry and ethics, and establish a scientific, transparent and inclusive normative framework for AI. Actively eliminate algorithmic bias, balance technical progress, risk prevention and social ethics, and make standards systems more inclusive and interoperable.

9. Public sectors first in deployment and application. The public sector of every country should lead and set an example in the application and governance of AI, giving priority to deploying reliable AI in public services such as healthcare, education and transport, and strengthening international exchange and cooperation. At the same time, the safety of such AI systems should be assessed regularly, and intellectual property such as patents and software copyright respected. Data and privacy protection must be strictly observed; lawful and orderly trading in training data should be actively explored; and the compliant opening and use of data should be advanced together, raising the standard of public administration and services.

10. Carry out AI safety governance. Assess AI risks in a timely way, propose targeted measures to prevent and respond to them, and build a safety-governance framework with broad consensus. Explore classified and tiered management, establish a system for AI risk testing and assessment, and advance mechanisms for sharing threat information and handling emergencies. Improve norms for data security and personal-information protection, and strengthen data-security management at stages such as the collection of training data and model generation. Increase investment in technical research and development, implement secure-development norms, and improve the explainability, transparency and safety of AI. Explore a traceability regime for AI services, to guard against the misuse and abuse of AI technology. Advocate open platforms for sharing best practices, and promote international cooperation on AI safety governance worldwide.

11. Jointly implement the Global Digital Compact. Actively implement the relevant commitments of the UN Pact for the Future and its annex, the Global Digital Compact; uphold the United Nations as the main channel; with the goals of helping developing countries bridge the digital divide and achieve fair and inclusive development, and on the basis of compliance with international law and respect for national sovereignty and differences in development, promote an inclusive, fair and multilateral system of global digital governance. Support establishing, within the UN framework, the two mechanisms of an international scientific panel on AI and a global dialogue on AI governance, and bringing them into operation as early as possible, so as to hold meaningful discussion of global AI governance, in particular of promoting the safe, fair and inclusive development of AI.

12. Strengthen international cooperation on AI capacity-building. Place international cooperation on AI capacity-building in a prominent position on the global AI governance agenda; encourage countries leading in AI to support developing countries in building comprehensive capacity in AI innovation, application and governance through practical actions such as cooperation on AI infrastructure, joint laboratories, jointly built platforms for mutual recognition of safety testing and evaluation, AI education and training for capacity-building, matchmaking events between AI supply and demand in industry, and joint construction of high-quality AI datasets and corpora. Jointly raise public AI literacy and skills, in particular safeguarding and strengthening the digital and intelligent rights and interests of women and children, and bridge the intelligence divide.

13. Build an inclusive governance model with participation from many parties. Support building inclusive governance platforms grounded in the public interest, in which actors of every kind take part together. Encourage AI enterprises of all countries to hold dialogue and exchanges, learn from one another’s application cases in different fields of AI, and advance cooperation on innovation, application, ethics and safety in specific fields and scenarios. Encourage research institutes, think tanks and international forums of every kind to build global and regional platforms for exchange and cooperation, so that the AI researchers, developers and governance authorities of all countries stay in technical and policy communication.
